# Unexecuted width-two negative scripts

The scripts are additive local experiment tooling, authored by
`/root/isometry_cli_tests`. Their author has not imported or executed them,
generated a mutant, or called the CLI/native checker. `candidate.md` and its
first `inputs.json` remain unchanged. `script-inputs.json` identifies this
later script preparation separately. No production, stdlib or original source
was modified.

Root supplied successful canonical width-two observations; the author read the
actual fixed-path result/association data afterward, without executing them:

The supplied results each record one actual native start and successful
client/native exit. The scripts require complete fixed-path raw client/native
records, mode/version/argv, file identity, absence of truncation/timeouts/wrapper
refusal, and retained payload/request binding. Recorder completion alone does
not satisfy the positive prerequisite. All hashes are file observations, not
compiled-HEAD or running-image attestations.

`generate_negatives.py` requires six explicit reviewed hash arguments. Its
barrier retains the canonical/original source inventories and binary guards,
the actual ten-file canonical prepared map, and both positive result hashes.
It resolves post-route D/M/P from the actual association, confirms the exact
last child/proof bindings and old recursive child position, and checks every
original nonroot row. Only after those checks does it create one-shot
`native-valid-negative-preparation-01/` under the authoring session. It emits
three payloads, three field-delta records, started/summary data and an eight-file
`prepared-files.json` map. It does not invoke a checker or copy original
payloads/requests into the new directory.

The actual association currently contains post D33/M33/P33 and E13; this
observation is not substituted for runtime association/header checks. The three
mutations remain the previously frozen phase, cancelled-real-reversal and high
H-to-X cases. All P/E rows and unrelated D/M rows remain unchanged. Original
QIRF bytes receive exactly one textual h-to-x replacement; parsed validation
requires the sole gate-field delta. Only the proposed finite description's
entries change to independently authored exact row-major X.

Root must review the actual generated data/map and obtain its SHA before
`capture_negatives.py`. That script adds the seventh explicit
`--negative-prepared-map-sha256` argument. Literal case/action paths select the
existing client and frozen logging forwarder; no map/payload field chooses a
command. Each of three cases gets one fresh inspection. Only a complete real
successful inspection permits a separate fresh unchanged n2 request call.
Failure records a skipped request and no semantic-negative claim. There are
at most six client observations, no retries and no repair of inputs or expected
outcomes. Each native forwarding invocation permits one actual native process;
an unexpected second attempt is retained and refused by the existing wrapper.

The fixed streaming helper retains actual raw argv/stdin/stdout/stderr/status,
caps streams at 1 MiB, and bounds the outer call at 55 seconds, with the existing
native 45-second and 5-second input budgets. Process groups differ; an outer
timeout does not attest that every descendant has stopped. Incomplete inner
records fail inspection success and remain operational uncertainty. The driver
records request outcomes honestly; `contract` does not identify an internal
phase/routing/H predicate uniquely. Its summary means capture completion only.

Use the literal scripts in this directory with the explicit hashes above plus
the independently reviewed script-map hash; the capture additionally needs
the subsequently observed negative prepared-map hash. Neither future hash is
predicted in this document. No maximum cases, new acceptance behavior, numerical
oracle, source-preservation or general Fourier proof, standard API, constitutional
guarantee, Issue completion or release claim follows from this preparation.
